title: Meridian AI evaluation playbook + scope review
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 4-week POC focused on quality/eval gating. Agreed on golden prompt set, regression harness, hallucination & format checks, scoring rubric, and a timeline with two benchmark runs. Discussed hosting options (hosted vs VPC), KMS requirements, and success criteria including hallucination thresholds and latency SLOs.
action_items: Alex Chen: Share draft golden prompts spreadsheet and template for regression harness by 2027-05-11
Priya Nair: Prepare benchmark runner config and baseline scripts, target run on 2027-05-16
Samir Khatri: Provide sample workload traces (1 week) and average token counts by 2027-05-12
Nora Blake: Confirm KMS/HSM requirements and SOC2 questions, return notes by 2027-05-13
Meridian: Identify stakeholder for final acceptance sign-off by 2027-05-14
next_steps: Send security pack + SOC2 summary link
Redwood to instrument two benchmark runs: baseline and tuned quantized model
Schedule call for benchmark review week of 2027-05-17
Start golden prompt labeling and rubric alignment
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-09 15:00 UTC - Duration ~63 minutes - Redwood: Alex/ Priya/ Diego - Meridian: Lena/ Samir/ Nora/ Chris

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — scope the POC, agree success criteria, workload and timing, and then the evaluation plan. does that look right?
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: Yup that works. we have about 6 weeks total budgeted but we wanted a 4-week focused POC if possible. main ask is to validate quality and hallucination behavior on our user prompts.
[00:22] Priya Nair: Great, we'll propose a 4-week run: week 1 instrument and collect golden prompts, week 2 run baseline benchmarks, week 3 apply optimizations and regression tests, week 4 finalize scoring and acceptance. Pretty standard but flexible.
[00:36] Samir Khatri: Quick constraint — we need keys and KMS in place, and data must not leave our VPC for the sensitive subset. can Redwood do a hybrid where PII goes to Private and generic workloads hit Hosted?
[00:50] Diego Ruiz: We can route by policy — that's fine. We usually set a tag on requests and route to Private Redwood nodegroup. There are a couple of network steps and we'll need your infra creds or a service account setup.
[01:05] Nora Blake: also SOC2 evidence, audit logs, and KMS/HSM details. we'll need to review the security pack before the benchmark runs.
[01:13] Alex Chen: we'll share the security pack and a short SOC2 summary link after the call, Priya will follow up on the KMS flow.
[01:20] Chris Park: for the evaluation itself, we care about: exact-match formatting for our structured outputs, hallucination rates on named entities, and semantic accuracy on intent classification. we also want latency numbers because some paths are user-facing.
[01:33] Priya Nair: ok so we'll build a quality eval that includes: 1) golden prompts set (canonical inputs + expected outputs), 2) regression harness that replays historical traces, 3) hallucination checks that compare named entities to a ground truth DB, 4) format validators for JSON/YAML outputs and 5) a scoring rubric that weights format and hallucination higher.
[01:52] Lena Ortiz: what does weighting look like? our main priority is correctness > latency.
[01:57] Priya Nair: Proposed scoring: 50% correctness (intent/slot), 30% hallucination penalty (lower is better), 10% format compliance (strict JSON schema), 10% latency and P95 SLO. We'll translate into pass/fail thresholds: overall score > 80 to pass, hallucination rate < 5%, JSON schema errors < 2% on golden set, p95 latency < 300ms for hosted and < 200ms for dedicated path.
[02:21] Samir Khatri: The p95 targets for hosted look ok but our internal SLA for private is 150ms. can we aim for 200ms?
[02:29] Diego Ruiz: We can tune batch sizes and KV cache warmup; private envs usually do better but depends on model variant and sequence lengths. we'll include token-length stratified benchmarks.
[02:40] Alex Chen: let's capture workload sizing: Samir can provide a week of traffic traces. For initial bench, we'll simulate steady 10 QPS and a 50/50 split of short (<=120 tokens) and long (<=1024 tokens) requests. Does that reflect reality?
[02:58] Samir Khatri: Yes that's close. peak bursts up to 40 QPS for short bursts. average tokens per request is about 180. monthly total tokens estimate around 1.2B.
[03:13] Priya Nair: That's helpful. For cost/throughput tradeoffs we'll run: baseline fp16 model, then int8 quantized variant, and a mid-range distilled variant. Benchmark matrix will include latency, cost per 1k tokens estimate, and quality metrics.
[03:29] Lena Ortiz: Distilled variant might fail some of our more complex prompts though, want to make sure we capture regression tests.
[03:35] Priya Nair: Exactly — regression harness will run your historical golden cases (we'll need labeled pairs) and flag items where score drops more than X points. we usually set X = 10 absolute points on the 0-100 scale for a failing regression, but we can adjust.
[03:49] Chris Park: can you show an example of a hallucination check?
[03:53] Diego Ruiz: Sure. we'll extract named entities from the model output, compare against your canonical entity list (provided by you), and then compute false positive rate. we also run a fuzzy-match for partial entity hits to reduce false alarms.
[04:08] Nora Blake: for PII we need redaction and a separate privacy lane — we'll supply a sample set that must never be logged. how do you handle no-logs for those?
[04:18] Alex Chen: we can route through Private with no persistent logs, and mask tokens at the proxy layer. we'll document the flow and share the runbook.
[04:25] Lena Ortiz: timeline check — when can you run the first benchmark?
[04:28] Priya Nair: If we get workload traces and golden prompts by 2027-05-12, we'll run baseline on 2027-05-16 and tuned run on 2027-05-23, then review on 2027-05-24. So about two benchmark windows in the 4-week POC.
[04:43] Samir Khatri: sounds good. what about acceptance sign-off?
[04:46] Alex Chen: acceptance is: pass golden set >=80, hallucination <5%, schema errors <2%, and no critical regressions. also a qualitative review from your product team.
[04:56] Chris Park: will Redwood provide tools for scoring or do we run locally?
[04:59] Priya Nair: We'll provide a reproducible scoring harness and a Jupyter notebook with results. the harness can run in your infra or ours; for private-sensitive prompts we'll run within your VPC.
[05:10] Lena Ortiz: any recommended size for the golden set?
[05:13] Diego Ruiz: We usually recommend 200-500 golden prompts for good coverage across intents and edge cases. for regressions a smaller golden core of ~50 with critical cases.
[05:24] Chris Park: ok we'll start with 250, and pick a 50-case critical subset.
[05:28] Priya Nair: For scoring, we'll also capture per-category metrics: intent F1, entity precision/recall, hallucination FP rate, schema error rate, and token cost. final report will include charts and per-case examples.
[05:40] Nora Blake: Regarding compliance, can you redact logs and provide encrypted audit logs to our SIEM?
[05:46] Alex Chen: yes encrypted logs with KMS keys and an audit export is standard for Private. we'll send the KMS runbook.
[05:52] Lena Ortiz: any blockers we should know about?
[05:54] Samir Khatri: infra time to set up service account and VPC peering might add a couple of days.
[05:59] Diego Ruiz: We'll provide a checklist to make that smooth.
[06:02] Alex Chen: good — recap and next steps: Redwood to share golden prompt template, security pack, and benchmark scripts; Meridian to deliver traces and golden set; target baseline run 2027-05-16.
[06:14] Lena Ortiz: sounds like a plan, thanks.
[06:18] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and action items.

Notes: references shared during call - Golden prompts template: https://redwood.internal/golden-prompts-template (placeholder link), Benchmark sheet: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/meridian-2027 (placeholder).

Transcript end.
